solution_summary: InMotion Inovasi Teknologi is an Indonesian-based technology company that builds software solutions for customer engagement across digital channels. As part of its continued development, the company migrated around 1,000 scripts from Amazon EC2 to Amazon CloudFront , leveraging Amazon S3 to distribute static content. By migrating the scripts to Amazon CloudFront, InMotion decreased its Amazon EC2 costs by 10 percent. business_outcome: Thanks to the speed and scalability of Amazon CloudFront, InMotion is helping large enterprises communicate with millions of customers in Bahasa Indonesia in a timelier manner. Today, around 50 of InMotion’s customers are using the 3Dolphins SRM suite to distribute over 15 million messages a day in Bahasa Indonesia as part of their customer engagement programs. Delivering messages on this scale in Bahasa Indonesia has given InMotion a significant advantage over competitors who also offer localized engagement tools.
metrics: As a result of the migration, the company reduced server costs by 10 percent and improved application performance by 30 percent.

evidence_quotes: Chief executive officer Sonny Hastomo, who co-developed the 3Dolphins solutions, says, “We wanted to offload script files from virtual server instances to lower our cloud costs as well as boost the performance of our applications.” In addition, the business sought to increase application scalability.

InMotion’s founders engaged with the company’s AWS account team, who proposed offloading the scripts which facilitated client-server communication into . “Our AWS team was proactive as always, listening to our objectives and providing the right solutions,” Hastomo says.
The company moved approximately 1,000 scripts for its 3Dolphins applications and chatbot service from Amazon EC2 instances to Amazon CloudFront, going live in two weeks.
InMotion also integrated Amazon CloudFront with Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), where it stores static assets such as imagery for web dashboards and chatbot interfaces.
Amazon CloudFront distributes the static content, caching the images at edge locations to reduce load time and protecting resources by checking content requests against access control lists.
